status.summary: No. 7 UFC featherweight (media panel, Nov 3, 2026) with a 21-4 pro record. He won a five-round main event over Melquizael Costa by unanimous decision (50-45, 50-45, 49-46; UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa, Las Vegas, May 16, 2026). He dropped Costa in round 1 and went 7 for 7 on takedowns with 9:28 of control, though Costa landed 33 leg strikes. That followed a decision loss to Jean Silva at UFC 324 (Jan 24, 2026; 27-30, 28-29, 28-29), his first fight after an 18-month layoff. He was then booked against Aaron Pico at UFC 333 (Oct 24, 2026, Abu Dhabi) but withdrew injured in September: Cageside Press, crediting MMA Fighting, said he had been having ongoing treatment for past injuries and could not heal in time (no body part named). Pico fought Losene Keita instead. No new booking as of Nov 6, 2026 (UFCalendar; ESPN lists only his previous fight). He is 2-3 in his last five, with all three losses on the scorecards (Max Holloway 2023, Movsar Evloev 2024, Silva 2026). Age 32.

style.summary: A southpaw boxer who fights at range and has never been knocked down in 15 UFC fights. He is hard to take down (73% career) and has two guillotine wins, and lately he has mixed in takedowns of his own. But his output is below the division average, and fighters who out-volume him or chop his legs (Holloway, Silva, and Costa for stretches) have won the striking.

moves.notes: Target split from fighters.json: decayed significant attempts are 82% head, 12% body, 6% legs (landed 74/16/10); career 83/12/5, against a featherweight league of 76/14/9.5. So head punches carry the weight, with body weights a little below a typical featherweight's and leg weights low. Knees and elbows are near zero because only 3% of decayed landed strikes come in the clinch. For a southpaw, 'jab' is the lead right hand and 'cross' the rear left; the cross is weighted just above the jab as a judgment, since ufcstats does not record technique and no scouting breakdown could be opened this pass. Spinning is zero.
